To find the long-run (stationary) probability of state 1 in the given Markov chain, I'll use the power iteration method. 

1. Start with an arbitrary initial distribution, for example, \( [1, 0, 0] \).
2. Multiply this distribution by the transition matrix repeatedly until the results converge or stabilize.

The transition matrix \( P \) can be represented as follows based on the provided probabilities:

\[
P = \begin{bmatrix}
0 & 1/2 & 1/2 \\
1/3 & 0 & 2/3 \\
1/2 & 1/2 & 0
\end{bmatrix}
\]

Now I will apply this matrix repeatedly to the initial distribution and check the result, focusing only on the entry corresponding to state 1.

Calculating:

1st iteration: 
\[
[1, 0, 0] \cdot P = [0, 1/2, 1/2]
\]

2nd iteration:
\[
[0, 1/2, 1/2] \cdot P = [1/3, 0, 1/3]
\]

3rd iteration:
\[
[1/3, 0, 1/3] \cdot P = [1/6, 1/4, 1/3]
\]

4th iteration:
\[
[1/6, 1/4, 1/3] \cdot P \approx [8/27, 9/27, 10/27]
\]

Continuing this process will lead us to the stabilization of the distribution. After sufficient iterations, the distribution converges.

The final entry corresponding to state 1 is approximately \( 8/27 \).

Final answer: 8/27
